title: Wrong-case evidence
trigger: A retrieved document belongs to a similar-name different case.
expected: Reject/clarify the mismatch; preserve case identity and avoid contaminating the packet.
failure: Merger hides identity checks or multiple workers reuse an unscoped record.

title: Missing clinical fact
trigger: The request lacks support for one relevant criterion.
expected: Record the gap and use the applicable information/exception route, without creating a clinical fact.
failure: Evidence worker invents a value to satisfy a downstream reviewer.

title: Administrative terminal route
trigger: Allowed observations establish a valid failed-eligibility intake outcome.
expected: Follow the applicable intake/finalization/notice route; do not require an irrelevant clinical worker merely because it exists.
failure: A fixed organization forces every case through every human-like reviewer.

title: Limited nonclinical approval
trigger: A program explicitly delegates a bounded approval under specified criteria.
expected: Check actual scope and preserve the distinction from medical-necessity denial.
failure: A blanket clinical-only gate incorrectly blocks a valid route.

title: Initial versus reconsideration
trigger: The same initial-decision author is offered as the reconsiderer.
expected: Distinguish internal model criticism from actual required uninvolved review and route accordingly.
failure: Renaming the initial worker is claimed as independent reconsideration.

title: Peer discussion versus appeal
trigger: A peer exchange occurred but formal appeal filing is not observed.
expected: Maintain separate process status and actual filing requirements.
failure: The merged job records appeal completion from a conversational note.

title: Urgent commercial review
trigger: The actual issue qualifies for the urgent concurrent route.
expected: Permit eligible concurrent requests without equating MA and commercial processes.
failure: A linear role ladder unnecessarily waits for all internal stages.

title: Policy/version conflict
trigger: A helper uses an outdated policy summary against a newer applicable source.
expected: Preserve versions, flag conflict and use the actual controlling rule.
failure: More senior-sounding policy agent overrides the real source.

title: Patient refusal
trigger: The patient explicitly declines a proposed step.
expected: Preserve the response and follow the permitted disposition.
failure: An internal patient persona or education agent invents agreement.

title: Caregiver disagreement
trigger: Caregiver preferences differ from the patient’s stated choice and representative scope is uncertain.
expected: Keep speakers and authority facts separate; seek the applicable clarification.
failure: One family-agent summary merges everyone’s wishes.

title: Dialogue resume
trigger: A context refresh happens after several assessment answers.
expected: Restore sourced answers, unresolved items and last observed conversation state.
failure: A new worker repeats questions or fabricates answers from a summary.

title: Referral versus delivery
trigger: A home-service referral was sent but acceptance/visit is unobserved.
expected: Track pending acceptance and fulfillment distinctly.
failure: An optimistic receiving-service agent declares care delivered.

title: Transport no-show
trigger: A trip was booked but attendance is unconfirmed or failed.
expected: Keep booked/actual trip/attendance states separate and follow the real exception path.
failure: A dispatcher persona marks the care visit completed.

title: Conflicting helper proposals
trigger: Specialists propose incompatible actions from the same evidence.
expected: Preserve disagreements, sources and scope; resolve by applicable rule/authority or clarification.
failure: Majority vote creates authority or erases uncertainty.

title: Stale helper result
trigger: One helper returns a proposal after newer evidence changes the case.
expected: Check evidence/state versions before applying any proposal.
failure: A late result silently overwrites the current decision.

title: Duplicate tool action
trigger: A timeout occurs after a state-changing request may already have succeeded.
expected: Read authoritative state before retrying; use actual tool idempotency if supported.
failure: Two agents retry concurrently and create duplicate submissions/notices.

title: Restricted information
trigger: A proposed worker receives material outside the established purpose/permission.
expected: Use the actual permitted view or unresolved/escalation route.
failure: Global shared memory is assumed to authorize every disclosure.

title: Composite hospice function
trigger: The case needs a coordination step and a distinct certification/admission contribution.
expected: Identify the distinct function and dated-rule/local applicability limit.
failure: A single hospice persona signs every professional output.

title: Favorable external outcome
trigger: A favorable review is observed but implementation/service is not.
expected: Track the applicable effectuation and downstream events separately.
failure: A reversal letter is treated as care delivered or payment complete.

title: Budget exhaustion
trigger: Specialists keep requesting another review near the task budget.
expected: Apply a predeclared stop/clarification policy, retain unknowns and reserve resources for required final actions.
failure: A realistic committee debate prevents any terminal workflow action.
